en.headline: Man in his 70s loses nearly HK$18 million in YouTube investment scam
en.dek: Police said the victim was lured by an online advertisement into a fake cryptocurrency platform and transferred large sums of USDT and ether before realising he had been defrauded.
body: A man in his seventies lost nearly HK$18 million after responding to a YouTube investment advertisement, police said in a CyberDefender alert.

The man left his contact details after seeing the ad in June. He was then contacted by someone posing as an investment adviser and invited into a WhatsApp group managed by an assistant. Discussions about virtual-currency profits prompted him to open accounts and begin investing.

Two months later he was directed to a second platform promising higher returns. Between August and October he transferred the equivalent of more than HK$18 million in USDT and ether to wallets supplied by the fraudsters. He managed to withdraw about HK$800,000 worth of USDT once before further withdrawals were refused.

Police said they had received more than 40 similar investment-scam reports in the past week, with total losses approaching HK$50 million. They urged the public not to trust online investment advertisements or self-styled advisers and never to transfer cryptocurrency to unknown addresses.

zh.headline: 七旬男子誤信YouTube投資廣告 損失近1800萬元
zh.dek: 警方表示，事主今年6月見到廣告後被引入假虛擬貨幣平台，8至10月間轉出逾1800萬港元等值USDT及以太幣，最終無法提款。
body: 警方在「守網者」社交平台公布，一名七旬男子因誤信YouTube投資廣告，損失近1800萬港元。
事主今年6月見到廣告後留下聯絡資料，自稱「投資顧問」的人士主動聯絡，安排他加入由「投資助理」管理的WhatsApp群組。群組內討論虛擬貨幣獲利，事主遂開設帳戶開始投資。
兩個月後被推介另一個聲稱回報更高的平台。8至10月間，事主按指示將逾1800萬港元等值的USDT及以太幣轉至騙徒提供的電子錢包。他一度成功提取約80萬港元等值USDT，其後提款被拒，始知受騙。
警方指過去一周接獲逾40宗同類投資騙案，總損失近5000萬港元，呼籲市民切勿輕信網上投資廣告及自稱投資顧問的人士，亦不要將虛擬貨幣轉至不明地址。
